configs.description: CRS312-4C+8XG-RM - eight 10G RJ45 ports, four combo 10G RJ45 / SFP+ ports, one 10/100 management port, the RJ45 console and a USB type A port. It has two built-in AC supplies and four fans. The box holds two IEC cords, a screw and feet kit (K57) and rack ears.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: No held document shows the rear: no rear view in the dimensions drawing, none in the one studio photograph, none in the NetBox files. The rear is left empty and no AC inlet is placed, so the DCIM export carries no power port. The product page counts two AC inputs.
gaps.wanted: A rear photograph or drawing showing the two AC inlets.

gaps.note: The drawing's side view shows the left wall as plain (a screw and two small holes), and it is left empty.
The right wall's vent field is read off the drawing's isometric view, which is not orthographic, so its size and position are estimated.
gaps.wanted: A right side view of the unit.

gaps.note: The brochure gives 64 MB RAM and 16 MB flash; the product page gives 128 MB RAM and 32 MB flash. Both are kept in the attrs as worded.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of which revision is current.

gaps.note: The brochure and the product page say USB type A, with a 1 A maximum, and state no USB generation. The port is drawn with the library's USB-A part, whose tongue is its default blue; photograph 1825 shows a pale tongue, so the colour is not the photograph's.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's USB generation for the port.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the product page and the quick guide for an LED table: none. The lamps carry the component's own vocabulary and no meaning is stated for the jack lamps or for USER, FAULT, POWER 2 and POWER 1.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CRS312-4C+8XG-RM.

gaps.note: Neither the brochure, the product page nor the quick guide gives a weight.
The saved product page carries no Discontinued badge and MikroTik publishes no end-of-life page, so no lifecycle is written.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The product page lists two AC inputs and four fans; the brochure says it has a dual power supply for redundancy; the quick guide says two alternating current inputs with IEC power connectors and four cooling fans with automatic speed control. No document held shows a removable supply module or gives a supply part number, so the supplies are part of the chassis and there are no bays, as on juniper/ex2300-24t. The fans are inside; the only opening the drawing shows for them is the vent field in the right wall.

buttons.note: One round button printed RESET (quick guide: the RouterBOOT reset button). Its centre is the drawing's.

chassis.note: 443 wide, 44 high, 183 deep: the drawing dimensions 443, 183 and 44 and the brochure and the product page print the same. The 6 mm the plan dimensions is the two cable loops standing off the rear, an accessory and not part of the depth. 443 is the body between the ear folds.

colour.note: median of photograph 1825's face (#c4c4ca); the jack plates are the photograph's #bcbdbd.

console.note: The RJ45 serial port (brochure: serial port RJ45) is the upper jack of the housing under the printed CONSOLE; the lower jack is the 10/100 management port, printed MGMT/BOOT (brochure: one 10/100 Ethernet port).

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code CRS312-4C+8XG-RM, one 10/100 port, eight 1G/2.5G/5G/10G RJ45 ports, four combo 10G Ethernet / SFP ports, AC 100 - 240 V with a redundant supply, USB type A, serial RJ45, 443 x 183 x 44 mm, -30 to +70 C, 60 W maximum power consumption, two IEC cords, a screw and feet kit (K57) and rack ears. The product page agrees on the dimensions, the AC input range, 60 W, the ports and the -30 to 70 C tested range, and adds two AC inputs and four fans. The two documents disagree on the platform: the brochure gives 64 MB RAM and 16 MB flash, the page 128 MB RAM, 32 MB flash and RouterOS v7; both are kept in the attrs as worded. The quick guide adds that each combo port has two physical connectors of which only one can be used at a time.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (brochure and product page, Included parts: Rack ears; the quick guide: 1U rackmount bracket, fitted to both sides with four screws). The drawing's side view shows the ear plate at the front end of the body, on the face, and the plan shows no ears (443 is the body), so the shipped position is flush. The K57 kit is a screw and feet kit and not a rack kit, so no kit is listed. The ears are not drawn.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Three jack plates 65.3 mm wide, 14.5 mm tall, top at 20.7 mm, at 12.8, 81.7 and 151.0 mm (69.1 mm step), four jacks each on a 15.9 mm pitch with the first 0.8 mm inside its plate (13.6, 82.7 and 151.8 mm), top at 21.35 mm. The SFP+ block is 30.4 x 26.7 at 221.3 mm, top 8.7 mm, two cages by two (14.5 x 10.0 each on a 15.1 mm column pitch and 14.0 mm row pitch, as the registry cage). The console housing holds two jacks, 18.1 mm wide at 256.3 mm, top 8.9 mm, the upper jack the CONSOLE and the lower the MGMT/BOOT, turned the other way up. The RESET button is at 278.8, 31.0 mm, the USB-A port stands on end centred at 287.7, 27.75 mm, and four lamp circles at 296.8 mm, 16.3, 21.3, 26.2 and 31.3 mm. The zigzag vent band over the jacks is the drawing's, 18.2 to 211.3 mm, 5.5 to 16.1 mm.

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body is 1163 px wide in the 200 dpi render for the printed 443 (2.624 px per mm) and 115 px tall, which reads 43.8 mm for the printed 44, 0.5 percent apart, so every x and y below is taken at 2.624 px per mm from the body's top-left corner of the front view. The four jacks of a block read a 15.9 mm pitch.

lamps.note: The jacks carry their own two lamps each (the library's Ethernet jack). The quick guide holds no LED table and the brochure none, so what a lamp shows is a gap.

legends-and-colours.note: Photograph 1825 prints 1 to 8 under the eight jacks, 1T to 4T under the combo jacks, 2F and 4F over the upper cages and 1F and 3F under the lower ones, 10G ETHERNET beside each plate, 10G COMBO over the third plate and SFP+ beside the cages. The combo jacks and cages sit on a light blue bracket. The jack plates read #bcbdbd and the face #c4c4ca in the photograph's medians. The positions of the legends are taken from the photograph's proportions and are estimated, good to about 1 mm. The USER, FAULT, POWER 2 and POWER 1 lamps are given the lit colours the photograph shows (green, red, blue, blue).

port-numbering.note: The metal prints 1 to 8 for the 10G jacks and 1T to 4T and 1F to 4F for the combo pairs; the quick guide says RouterOS shows them as combo 1 to 4. The copper jacks are named copper-1 to copper-4 and the cages cage-1 to cage-4, with the same numbers: the group says they are one port at a time. The upper cage of the left column is printed 2F and the lower 1F, so cage-1 is the lower one.

rear-layout.note: No held document shows the rear: the drawing has no rear view, its isometric hides the rear, the one studio photograph looks at the front, and the NetBox files carry no rear. The rear is left empty and the two AC inlets are not placed; no other model's rear is used. The export therefore carries no power port, though the product page counts two AC inputs.

side-layout.note: The drawing's side view is the left wall (plain: a screw, two small holes, ear plate at the front). The isometric shows the right wall with a rectangular hexagon vent field; it is not an orthographic view, so the field is read as a fraction of the wall (from 25 to 119 mm behind the front, 4.4 to 27.4 mm down) and is estimated, good to about 5 mm. The left wall is drawn empty.
